kings1.8.p1.b1.text: At that time Solomon assembled before him in Jerusalem the elders of Israel—all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites—to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.

kings1.8.p1.b2.text: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,

kings1.8.p1.b3.text: … and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings.

kings1.8.p1.b4.text: There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.

kings1.8.p2.b1.text: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.

kings1.8.p2.b2.text: The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place …

kings1.8.p2.b3.text: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of the land of Egypt.

kings1.8.p3.b1.text: And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD

kings1.8.p3.b2.text: so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

kings1.8.p4.b1.text: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud. I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”

kings1.8.p4.b2.text: And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all

kings1.8.p4.b3.text: … it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

kings1.8.p4.b4.text: Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke … I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

kings1.8.p5.b1.text: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,

kings1.8.p5.b2.text: and said: “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below, keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.

kings1.8.p5.b3.text: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk before Me as you have done.’

kings1.8.p5.b4.text: And now, O God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant, my father David.

kings1.8.p6.b1.text: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth?

kings1.8.p6.b2.text: Even heaven, the highest heaven, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.

kings1.8.p6.b3.text: May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day … so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.

kings1.8.p6.b4.text: … Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.

kings1.8.p7.b1.text: When a man sins against his neighbor … and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple, then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants …

kings1.8.p7.b2.text: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You … then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel …

kings1.8.p7.b3.text: When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place …

kings1.8.p7.b4.text: … then may You hear from heaven … May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.

kings1.8.p8.b1.text: When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers,

kings1.8.p8.b2.text: or when their enemy besieges them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,

kings1.8.p8.b3.text: … whatever prayer or petition Your people Israel make—each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple …

kings1.8.p8.b4.text: … be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive … since You know his heart …

kings1.8.p9.b1.text: And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your name—

kings1.8.p9.b2.text: … then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place … Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel,

kings1.8.p9.b3.text: When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to the LORD in the direction of the city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,

kings1.8.p9.b4.text: then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.

kings1.8.p10.b1.text: When they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,

kings1.8.p10.b2.text: ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’

kings1.8.p10.b3.text: … when they pray to You in the direction of the land … and the house I have built for Your Name, then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and petition, and may You uphold their cause.

kings1.8.p10.b4.text: For they are Your people and Your inheritance; You brought them out of Egypt, out of the furnace for iron.

kings1.8.p11.b1.text: Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.

kings1.8.p11.b2.text: And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:

kings1.8.p11.b3.text: “Blessed be the LORD … Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses.

kings1.8.p11.b4.text: May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us nor forsake us.

kings1.8.p11.b5.text: So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day …

kings1.8.p12.b1.text: Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.

kings1.8.p12.b2.text: And Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep.

kings1.8.p12.b3.text: On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD … since the bronze altar before the LORD was too small …

kings1.8.p12.b4.text: So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.

kings1.8.p13.b1.text: So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him—a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt—kept the feast before the LORD our God for seven days and seven more days—fourteen days in all.

kings1.8.p13.b2.text: On the fifteenth day Solomon sent the people away. So they blessed the king

kings1.8.p13.b3.text: … and went home, joyful and glad in heart for all the good things that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
